condition: Local anesthetic systemic toxicity (LAST) with neurologic and cardiovascular toxicity
evaluationParameters: Continuous cardiac rhythm and hemodynamic response, including ventricular ectopy and blood pressure.
Neurologic and respiratory status, including seizure cessation, level of consciousness, oxygenation, and ventilation.
missingInformation: Specific local anesthetic, concentration, infusion rate, total dose, and whether an inadvertent bolus or intravascular administration occurred
Client weight for weight-based lipid emulsion dosing
Current oxygen saturation, respiratory effort, airway patency, and end-tidal carbon dioxide
Whether the seizure is ongoing and whether pulses remain present
priorityActions: Stop the local anesthetic infusion immediately and disconnect the peripheral nerve catheter from the infusion source.
Initiate the local anesthetic systemic toxicity emergency protocol, including prompt administration of 20% lipid emulsion while supporting airway, ventilation, and circulation.
reasoning: The rapid progression from classic neurologic prodromes during local anesthetic administration to seizure, ventricular dysrhythmia, and hypotension is characteristic of severe LAST. Immediate removal of the anesthetic source, lipid-emulsion-based resuscitation, and close cardiovascular and neurologic-respiratory evaluation are priorities.
